svg.title: TOPAK I3 — FloorComposition.tla: nothing is admitted without a clean floor permit, whatever the bundle says, and the bundle cannot write what the floor reads. Five invariants, each with the mutations that break it: checked by TLC, proved by TLAPS and in Lean
svg.desc: The module ADR-0030 §9 reports, drawn from its own text and from every results file about it, all read at build time: the decision, the floor's four policies and the havoc bundle, the five properties and the section each states, the mutation matrix, the witnesses, ADR-0030 §9's table compared row by row, every theorem and lemma, the certified run, the Lean encoding, mirror and graph check, and the model of the code's decision that refines it. What is checked or proved here is checked or proved of the module, at its constants or by its proofs: one small floor text and havoc bundles, not Cedar, not the floor in force and not the reference (ADR-0030 §9, Scope). The module is frozen, cited by digest (ADR-0030 §9, ADR-0046, ADR-0053).

svg.text: Checked, proved and certified mean what ADR-0046 §1 says: TLC checks the mutations and witnesses at the module's constants; TLAPS proves each invariant under the hypothesis its statement names; the certified run accounts for every obligation by a route an independent checker accepted, or names LS4. Nothing here is said of the running reference.

text.tspan: The mechanism, as the module states it: an admit needs a clean floor permit and an affirmative bundle allow, and every decision records what it did against each property
What each decision records: one flag per property

svg.text: set when an admit had no clean floor permit
set when an admit came with an engine error
set when an admit had no bundle allow
set when an admit lies outside Envelope, stated on truth
① the slice may drop owner or sealed: a fault §4 forbids, modelled so that §1 holds without it
② FloorPermit: the engine allows and no policy errored (ADR-0030 §1). M_ERR takes the engine's decision, errors
③ BundleDeny: anything but allow denies (§1). M_FAILOPEN denies only on deny.
④ Admit is ② and not ③. M_OVERRIDE admits on a bundle allow alone.

text.tspan: The floor: four policies, evaluated with Cedar's rules (the module's header)
P2 permit Draft when resource.owner == principal
P3 permit Emit when resource.owner == principal

svg.text: "any satisfied forbid denies; else any satisfied permit allows; else deny. A policy whose condition reads a missing attribute errors and is SKIPPED"

svg.text: Reassign(t, s) (line 69) and Seal(t) (line 74) write fstore and the ghost truth together.
BundleWrite(t, s) (line 81) writes fstore alone, and is enabled only under M_WRITE.
BundleCannotWriteFloorInputs: fstore = truth, the floor reads only what the lift wrote

text.tspan: OwnerIs(e, p) == IF e.owner = NONE THEN "ERR" ELSE IF e.owner = p THEN "T" ELSE "F"
SealedIs(e) == IF e.sealed = NONE THEN "ERR" ELSE IF e.sealed = "yes" THEN "T" ELSE "F"
IF a = "Draft" THEN OwnerIs(e, p) ELSE "F",
IF a = "Emit" THEN OwnerIs(e, p) ELSE "F" }
Forbids(e, a) == { IF a = "Emit" THEN SealedIs(e) ELSE "F" }
The engine, and the floor's permit

a.tspan: EngineAllow(e, p, a) == ("T" \notin Forbids(e, a)) /\ ("T" \in Permits(e, p, a))
EngineErr(e, p, a) == ("ERR" \in Forbids(e, a)) \/ ("ERR" \in Permits(e, p, a))

text.tspan: IF Mut = "M_ERR" THEN EngineAllow(e, p, a)
ELSE EngineAllow(e, p, a) /\ ~EngineErr(e, p, a)

svg.text: ADR-0030 §1: a permit with an error is not a permit.

text.tspan: BundleDeny(b) == IF Mut = "M_FAILOPEN" THEN b = "deny" ELSE b # "allow"
IF Mut = "M_OVERRIDE" THEN FloorPermit(e, p, a) \/ b = "allow"

svg.text: Composition is monotone: the bundle can only subtract.

The floor errors: FloorErrorIsDeny is not met by an engine that never errs.

svg.text: "FloorRefinement proves the code's decision a Decide step of spec/lean's re-encoding of FloorComposition.tla, on the engine premise T-0045-3 (Cedar's rule over the module's four policies) and with the module's own lift; it is not a refinement of the floor in force, and
That Cedar decides as the module's three-valued evaluation does: the engine premise, T-0045-3.
Anything of the floor in force: one four-policy floor text is modelled, and the floor in force is Genesis-provisional (ADR-0030 A3).
The trusted base: a component enters only if its failure can only subtract, or its identity is issued
